body:
Machine A: Rut's decisions on the B5-20 engine asks. Guiding principle from Rut: remove as much complexity as possible now. Features can be added later.

1. Stored AWA (Adaptive Wide Angle) recipe op: YES only if it is very easy. Concretely, it must fit the existing smart-filter parameter storage with no new document-format/contract version and no migration. If it needs a new persisted op type or a contract bump, don't do it. Ship AWA as a destructive/baked filter instead, or defer it. Tell A which case applies before implementing.
2. Lifting the 16.7M-vertex mesh cap: NO. Keep the cap. If a warp would exceed it, use a coarser adaptive mesh or return a clear error.
3. GPU displacement: nothing new. Reuse the existing resident displacement renderer, the one Free/Warp/Perspective/Puppet already use, only where it drops in unchanged. Otherwise use the CPU path. No new GPU pipelines.
4. Lens dependency: only if it's a small lift, meaning EXIF focal length plus a couple of built-in projection models, with no new crate or C library and no lens database (lensfun's LGPL/CC-BY-SA licensing is a problem anyway). If it needs any external dependency or database, don't add it. AWA works from manual constraint lines.
5. Vanishing Point (plane storage and the feature itself): NO, not in B5-20. Defer entirely.
6. Engine-code ownership: YES. B may add self-contained engine modules for B5-20. They must be written tests-first and be independently reviewed by A before merge. Keep shared-file edits minimal. (document/vanishing.rs is moot since Vanishing Point is deferred.)

Please send a short B5-20 scope summary reflecting this before starting.
